summary: Winema NF lookout site: an 80-foot 1929 steel Aermotor tower, replaced in 1961 by a 20-foot timber tower; only remains today.

facts.design: 80-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7 x 7 cab (1929); replaced in 1961 by a 20-foot treated timber tower
facts.status_note: The 1961 timber tower is gone; a 2017 PeakBagging.com page says only the remains of the lookout are left.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Winema National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the 1929 living space a tent cabin; the Oregon Lookouts page gives a 12 by 16 ground cabin. The story reports both.

The steel tower was dismantled in 1961 (guide quoting Kresek's book), and the 20-foot timber tower came down after 1973 or 1974 (register and PeakBagging.com). These are two different structures, so the dates do not conflict.

notes_for_editor: The record's height_m 24.4 is the 1929 steel tower (80 ft); the last structure was 20 ft (about 6.1 m). No access level is set: no source read states whether the site is open to the public, so none is recorded. A climbing guide gives road directions and no closure notice was found, which does not establish open access. The 1928 letter in the Oregon Lookouts page places the mountain on the Klamath Indian Reservation; no source read says whether the summit is on tribal land today, so check before any access wording. The timber tower's removal is dated 'after 1974' (PeakBagging.com) against 'used for emergency in 1973' (register); the dates are reported as given. The 2017 photo is the most recent source; no source read describes the site after that. The 1937 truck-trail item and other 1968 entries on the Oregon Lookouts page were left out.
